data_problems: SCAN SELFTEST FAILED ON THE FIRST RUN - ROOT CAUSE MEASURED AND FIXED, AND THE SCAN RE-RUN. The first scan.py of this session printed 'scan SELFTEST FAIL - OCCL 30-Sep-2026 anti-dumping duty raise, generic subject: got []'. The cause was traced, not guessed: scan.classify falls back to the filing's PDF TEXT for a generic heading, via scan._text -> orderbook.pdf_text, which does 'import fitz' inside a try/except that swallows the failure and then WRITES THE EMPTY RESULT TO THE CACHE. PyMuPDF was absent, so the TRADE-from-body rule that exists precisely because of the OCCL miss (runbook/PLAYBOOK, 2026-10-12) was silently dead, AND 46 empty .txt files had been written into scripts/ideas/_cache which would have poisoned later reads in this run. Why it was absent: 'pip install pymupdf' reported exit 0 but /usr/bin/pip is Python 3.13's pip (/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/pip) while the interpreter is Python 3.11.17 at /usr/local/bin/python3 - the packages landed in a site-packages the interpreter never reads. Fixed with 'python3 -m pip install pymupdf xlrd'; all 46 empty cache files were deleted; scan.py was then re-run and printed 'scan SELFTEST PASS', and the committed scan/2026-10-22.json is that re-run. NOTE FOR THE OWNER, who maintains the scripts: the swallowed exception plus the empty-cache write is the actual defect - a missing PyMuPDF should be loud and should not be cached as 'this PDF has no text'. The routine's own step 0 ('python3 -c "import fitz" || pip install --quiet pymupdf') cannot catch it either, because the import test and the install use different Pythons; it needs to be 'python3 -m pip'.

note: Three lanes worked and three cards were published, and the day's most useful work was arguably the two things that were corrected rather than the three that were written. Lane one kept nothing of 53 PIB releases, which is the normal outcome and was not forced. Lane two had 39 strong groups but only a handful with evidence dated today, and the one taken - natural rubber, ranked ninth by composite strength - was chosen because the Rubber Board's Kottayam RSS4 print is a 6,872-reading daily series at its series high AND because the company itself names the price in its own press release, which is the playbook's test rather than the group's rank. Lane three gave eleven candidates, of which four were researched and three published; the two biggest-scoring names were opened and rejected on measured grounds - Magellanic Cloud's Rs 115 cr is an L1 bid, not an order, at 16.5% of consolidated sales from a filer with 19 order announcements on record, and Acme Universal's 'order' turned out to be Rs 70.18 LAKH. The two corrections: the order-book screen's one new row, TARIL at +281.8%, was a transcript misread - 'order in hand OR INQUIRIES' - where the same call's opening remarks give the real figure, Rs 7,237 cr, +31.6%, matching management's own '+32%'; and scan.py's selftest failure traced to PyMuPDF having been installed into the wrong Python, which had silently killed the generic-heading TRADE rule and written 46 empty files into the PDF-text cache. Both are documented in full above, the cache was cleared and the scan re-run to a PASS. What a reader should distrust about today: two of the three commodity panels are months old, so the signal ranking is not a ranking of today's news; X and ValuePickr were unreachable, so both social sections are search summaries with every post marked 'not read'; and Tinna's results statement is an unreadable scan, so that card's consolidated numbers come from a press release. All three are stated on the cards themselves, not only here. One card is published at LOW confidence on purpose: Fairchem Organics' earnings turnaround is real and computed line by line from the filing, but the business cannot be modelled physically from anything it discloses, the spread that produced it is undisclosed and demonstrably volatile, it trades Rs 8.6 lakh a day, and the same board meeting approved a Rs 12.01 cr land purchase from the Chairman and Managing Director with no valuation basis given.
